# Change AI credit columns to decimal

**Mixpost Enterprise only.** The `mixpost_e_ai_credits` and
`mixpost_e_ai_credit_transactions` tables ship with the Enterprise package — this
script does nothing on a Pro-only install.

Widens the Mixpost Enterprise AI credit columns from integer to `decimal(12,3)` so
balances can be tracked with fractional precision:

- `mixpost_e_ai_credits.balance`
- `mixpost_e_ai_credit_transactions.amount`
- `mixpost_e_ai_credit_transactions.balance_after`

## Why

Token usage is now converted to credits before deduction, so balances are no longer
whole numbers. This one-shot patch downloads a migration, applies **only** that
migration, then removes both the migration file and its row in the `migrations`
table — leaving no trace in your project. Existing whole-credit values are preserved
as-is, and `tokens_used` stays an integer because it counts tokens, not credits.

It is **safe to run more than once** — widening an already-decimal column is a no-op,
and the migration guards every table with `Schema::hasTable()`.

## Usage

### Docker

Open a shell inside the Mixpost container:

```bash
docker compose exec -it mixpost bash
```

The container's working directory is already the project root, so you can pipe the
script straight into bash:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh | bash
```

If your project root is somewhere else, pass it as an argument:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh | bash -s -- /var/www/html
```

### Without Docker

Run it from your project root:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh | bash
```

Or download, inspect, and run it:

```bash
curl -fsSL -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh
chmod +x change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh
./change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh            # uses the current directory
./change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh /var/www/html   # or pass the project root
```

## Output

```
Downloading migration...
Applying migration...
Removing migration bookkeeping...
Done. AI credit columns are now decimal(12,3).
```

<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

return new class extends Migration
{
    /**
     * Mixpost Enterprise only. AI credit balances are now tracked with fractional
     * precision (token usage is converted to credits before deduction). Widen the
     * credit columns from integers to decimals. Existing whole-credit values are
     * preserved as-is. `tokens_used` stays an integer because it counts tokens,
     * not credits.
     */
    public function up(): void
    {
        if (Schema::hasTable('mixpost_e_ai_credits')) {
            Schema::table('mixpost_e_ai_credits', function (Blueprint $table) {
                $table->decimal('balance', 12, 3)->default(0)->change();
            });
        }

        if (Schema::hasTable('mixpost_e_ai_credit_transactions')) {
            Schema::table('mixpost_e_ai_credit_transactions', function (Blueprint $table) {
                $table->decimal('amount', 12, 3)->change();
                $table->decimal('balance_after', 12, 3)->change();
            });
        }
    }
};

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Widen the Mixpost Enterprise AI credit columns from integer to decimal(12,3).
#
# For the Mixpost Enterprise package only (the `mixpost_e_ai_credits` and
# `mixpost_e_ai_credit_transactions` tables ship with Enterprise).
#
# AI credit balances are now tracked with fractional precision (token usage is
# converted to credits before deduction). This one-shot patch downloads a
# migration, applies only that migration, then removes both the migration file
# and its row in the `migrations` table so it leaves no trace in your project.
#
# Run once from your Mixpost Enterprise project root:
#   ./change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh
# Or pass the project root explicitly:
#   ./change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal.sh /var/www/html
#
# Safe to run more than once: widening an already-decimal column is a no-op, and
# the migration guards every table with Schema::hasTable().

set -euo pipefail

MIGRATION_NAME="2026_07_11_000000_change_ai_credits_columns_to_decimal"
MIGRATION_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/change-ai-credits-columns-to-decimal/${MIGRATION_NAME}.php"

APP_DIR="${1:-$(pwd)}"

if [ ! -f "$APP_DIR/artisan" ]; then
    echo "Error: '$APP_DIR' does not look like the project root." >&2
    echo "Run this from your project root, or pass the project root as the first argument." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Stage the migration in a throwaway directory so `migrate` runs only this one
# file and never touches other pending migrations. The trap removes the file on
# exit, so the migration itself is always cleaned up.
STAGING_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$STAGING_DIR"' EXIT

MIGRATION_FILE="$STAGING_DIR/${MIGRATION_NAME}.php"

echo "Downloading migration..."
curl -fsSL "$MIGRATION_URL" -o "$MIGRATION_FILE"

echo "Applying migration..."
php "$APP_DIR/artisan" migrate --path="$MIGRATION_FILE" --realpath --force

echo "Removing migration bookkeeping..."
php "$APP_DIR/artisan" tinker --execute="\Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB::table('migrations')->where('migration', '$MIGRATION_NAME')->delete();"

echo "Done. AI credit columns are now decimal(12,3)."

# Backfill Bluesky `provider_post_id`

Realigns the Bluesky pivot column `mixpost_post_accounts.provider_post_id` from the
record **CID** to the **AT-URI**, and moves the old CID into the pivot `data` payload
under a `cid` key.

## Why

Posts published before the analytics fix stored the record CID in
`provider_post_id`, while insights are keyed by the AT-URI (kept in the pivot
`data` payload). That mismatch left those posts without analytics. This script
fixes it.

It is **safe to run more than once** — rows that already point at the AT-URI are
skipped.

## Requirements

Mixpost Pro **v3.8.3** or newer. Check the version in Admin Console > System > Status.

## Usage

### Docker

Open a shell inside the Mixpost container:

```bash
docker compose exec -it mixpost bash
```

The container's working directory is already the project root, so you can pipe the
script straight into bash:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id.sh | bash
```

If your project root is somewhere else, pass it as an argument:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id.sh | bash -s -- /var/www/html
```

### Without Docker

Run it from your project root:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id.sh | bash
```

Or download, inspect, and run it:

```bash
curl -fsSL -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/scripts/main/mixpost/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id/backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id.sh
chmod +x backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id.sh
./backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id.sh            # uses the current directory
./backfill-bluesky-provider-post-id.sh /var/www/html   # or pass the project root
```

## Output

```
Backfilled 12 Bluesky post(s).
```

If there are no Bluesky accounts, you'll see:

```
No Bluesky accounts found. Nothing to backfill.
```
